composition: A: brief's first viewport as written. House cropped to the central three bays, headline in the snow under the steps, Choose a room plaque list begins below.
prompt: A mobile landing page at phone viewport, portrait, for Wander Niagara, rendered edge to edge as a real web page with crisp readable text, no phone frame, no browser chrome. The page is a house: the visitor is planning a winter day trip or overnight to St. Catharines and the Benchlands and picks a room to enter. Parts in reading order: a slim header on the night sky with a small white "Wander" wordmark at left and one small engraved brass door plaque button reading "What's on" at right. Below it a red-brick Georgian colonial house at night fills the full width, cropped to its central three bays so the two ground-floor windows, the black six-panel front door under its white arched portico with a wreath and a brass lantern, and the two dormers above are each large. Every window glows warm amber through sheer curtains with a single candle; the left window shows a crystal chandelier, the right window a lit Christmas tree. Warm-white mini-lights outline each window and the portico arch. Snow on the roof, sills and steps; slow falling snow. Set in the blue-shadowed snow beneath the steps, as set type: the headline "Winter is made for wandering" and the subline "A holiday escape to St. Catharines and the Benchlands." Below the snow a page section begins, titled "Choose a room", listing five engraved brass door plaques as a vertical list: "What's on this winter", "Eat, drink and shop", "Winter outdoors", "Stay the night", "Winter reading"; the list runs off the bottom edge. Visual law: the ground is a warm navy night sky, never black. Type is a heavy, friendly 1990 greeting-card serif in snow white. Buttons are small brass plaques with engraved lettering. Warm inside, cold outside; film-grain warmth.
